title: Anxiety disorders
lead: Anxiety, panic, phobias and fear of separation are disorders in which anxiety or fear becomes excessive and gets in the way of life; they are treated with psychotherapy and, when needed, with medication.

blocks.h: How does an anxiety disorder present?
blocks.sub: Anxiety and fear that last a long time, cannot be controlled and interfere with ordinary life

items.d: Worry covers many areas of life — work, family, health, daily topics — and is hard to control. There can also be “worry about worry.”
Sudden acute fear that peaks within a few minutes: palpitations, shortness of breath, a feeling of suffocation, fear of death or of losing control. An attack lasts 5–20 minutes.
Muscle tension, fatigue, sleep disturbance, sweating, dry mouth, headache.

The person avoids situations from which escape is difficult or where help may not be available: transport, crowds, leaving home alone. “Safety” behaviors often appear — a companion, a phone, medication carried along.
Intense and persistent fear of negative evaluation or humiliation by others. The body responds with flushing, tremor, sweating, voice tremor.

items.t: Fear of separation and silence in children
items.d: The child fears separation from a close person or from home, refuses to sleep away from home, avoids school. Or consistently stays silent in certain situations, such as school, while speaking normally at home.

blocks.h: Which disorders belong to this group?
blocks.sub: ICD-11, anxiety or fear-related disorders, codes 6B00–6B06

items.d: Excessive, hard-to-control anxiety about many things that lasts at least several months and comes with tension, fatigue and sleep disturbance.
Recurrent, unexpected panic attacks and persistent worry about their recurrence.
Excessive fear and avoidance of situations from which escape is difficult or help may not be available.
Marked, irrational fear and avoidance of a specific object or situation; the person usually recognizes the fear as excessive.
Intense and persistent fear of negative evaluation or humiliation by others in social situations.
Developmentally inappropriate excessive fear and anxiety related to separation from an attachment figure (typically a parent) or home.
Consistent failure of a child to speak in specific situations, such as school, while speaking normally in others, such as home.

blocks.h: When should you see a doctor?
blocks.sub: By the criteria a doctor uses
items: Anxiety is directed at many areas of life, is present most of the time for several months, and is hard to control.
Alongside the anxiety there is restlessness, easy fatigue, difficulty concentrating, irritability, muscle tension or sleep disturbance.
Anxiety or fear causes significant distress or gets in the way of work, study or relationships.
You avoid places and situations because you fear an attack.
Before a diagnosis, the doctor rules out another cause: the effect of a substance or a medical condition — for example, checks the thyroid, the heart, and the use of caffeine or stimulants.

blocks.sub: The basis is psychotherapy; medication is added when indicated

items.d: The method with the strongest evidence base in generalized anxiety; 12–20 sessions.
list: testing beliefs about anxiety
working with intolerance of uncertainty
exposure — gradually stopping the avoidance of anxiety-provoking situations
problem-solving training
relaxation — progressive muscle relaxation, diaphragmatic breathing

items.d: Gradually approaching avoided situations — a first-line method.
list: in agoraphobia — graded in vivo exposure and cognitive restructuring
in specific phobia — a single 2–3-hour structured exposure session is effective for most animal and situational phobias
in blood-injection phobia — applied tension: the person is taught to tense the muscles, which prevents fainting
virtual reality exposure — an alternative; the evidence base is developing

items.d: CBT with a large effect; 12–16 sessions.
list: psychoeducation
interoceptive exposure — building tolerance to bodily sensations without catastrophizing
in vivo exposure
cognitive restructuring

items.d: Individual CBT is first-line; 12–16 sessions. Individual CBT is superior to group CBT.
list: redirecting self-focused attention
video feedback
behavioral experiments
cognitive restructuring and exposure

items.d: CBT with parental involvement and a behavioral approach.
list: in separation anxiety, parental involvement in CBT is critical; the return to school is graded
frequent phone calls and visits (accommodation) strengthen symptoms
in selective mutism — graded exposure and gradual introduction of a stranger, coordination with the teacher
the parent stops speaking for the child

items.d: SSRIs and SNRIs are first-line.
list: the effect is assessed at 4–6 weeks; a full response may take 8–12 weeks
treatment starts at a low dose: a temporary increase in anxiety is possible in the first days
benzodiazepines — only in the acute period, for no more than 2–4 weeks; the dependence potential is high
after remission, treatment continues for at least 12 months; discontinuation is gradual, and abrupt cessation raises the risk of relapse

items.d: An addition to the main treatment.
list: limiting caffeine
regular physical activity
sleep hygiene
avoiding alcohol and psychoactive substances

blocks.sub: A single session or a monthly package — we choose the format together

items: Is anxiety a normal feeling or an illness?
There is a clinical distinction between normal anxiety and a disorder: severity, duration, uncontrollability, somatic components and functional impairment. A diagnosis is made by specific criteria.
Can you learn not to worry by willpower?
No. Generalised anxiety disorder is a neurobiological dysregulation; CBT or medication acts at the neurobiological level.
No. Benzodiazepines are used only short-term, for 2–4 weeks, because the dependence potential is high. SSRIs and SNRIs are first-line.
SSRIs and SNRIs are also effective in anxiety disorders — through the effect of the serotonergic system on amygdala activity.
Will I have to take antidepressants for life?
No. After remission, treatment continues for 12 months, then gradual discontinuation is possible; if there is a relapse, treatment is restarted.
